Live Unreal MCP showcase — October 11–12, 2026

The authorized demonstration creates one separate Blueprint asset in ForgeMCPDev. It demonstrates native Blueprint authoring through the connected Codex MCP host, with reviewed preview/apply, compilation, saving, native read-back and editor opening. It does not place an actor or save/change the open TestArea world.

Inspect in Unreal

The host confirmed the asset editor opened for /Game/ForgeMCP_Demos/BP_MCP_Showcase_20261011. Find it under Content → ForgeMCP_Demos if the tab is closed.

  • Components: DemoMesh, a native StaticMeshComponent (no mesh assigned).
  • Variables: DemoEnabled = true, DemoLabel = Created through ForgeMCP.
  • Function: EchoValue, a pure function with float InputValue and OutputValue. The input is wired directly to the return output; this is a graph-authoring example.
  • Compilation: native apply reported zero compiler errors and zero warnings.

The host rejected a wrong preview confirmation, replay of the consumed preview and duplicate creation at the same package path. It also inspected the existing wooden box and sphere transforms and the wooden-box component's static-mesh reference. Those world actors were read only.

Repeat the read-only acceptance

Rediscover sessions first and substitute the current explicit session ID. Process IDs are temporary. The verifier requires the exact local ForgeMCPDev project and the previously saved showcase asset. It never creates, compiles or saves content.

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/verify_unreal_showcase_mcp.py --session-id unreal-27496

Use --report Saved/ForgeMCPShowcase/<new-name>.json to retain a new token-free report. Existing reports are never overwritten. Failed checks exit unsuccessfully.

The verifier launches a fresh source MCP stdio subprocess, discovers the tool registry and checks exact project identity, initialized variables, component class, both sides of the function pin link, native Asset Registry presence, unchanged project/world context and unchanged package checksum. The October 11 run found 85 tools and verified the 31,863-byte package with SHA-256 7e8d94f63008e238e5c687931c3da13788fe8e044ff0b10f4b475b9dfbad34f1.

Evidence and limits

  • Saved/ForgeMCPShowcase/20261011-connected-host.json: connected-host creation, compiler/inspection result, recipe and guard-check results.
  • Saved/ForgeMCPShowcase/20261011-readback.json: independent source stdio read-back.
  • Full Python regression suite: 288 passed; Ruff: passed.
  • Saved/ForgeMCPShowcase/20261012-editor-build.log: successful full ForgeMCPDevEditor build after the user saved/closed the Editor. Project/runtime DLLs linked and target metadata completed. The initial open-editor attempt failed with LNK1104; the closed-editor retry succeeded.
  • Saved/ForgeMCPShowcase/20261012-fresh-editor-readback.json: all seven read-back checks passed after reopening Unreal in a fresh process, with the same package checksum and saved graph. Windows module enumeration also confirmed the fresh Editor loaded the rebuilt plugin DLL from this checkout.

The native response confirms asset opening; no screenshot or interactive visual QA was performed. PIE execution and calling the function in gameplay remain unverified. Saved-package loading in a fresh Editor process passed. Discovery of 85 tools does not prove every operation works. Material, GAS, DataAsset, transfer and broader roadmap workflows retain their separate acceptance gates. No distribution or release is implied.
